title: Concept Maps as a Content and Language Integrated Learning Facilitator in Digital Gaming Contexts - Triangulated Evidence From Students' Learning Achievements, Perceptions and Behavioural Patterns

segments.sourceText: ABSTRACT Background: While both Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) and Digital Game-Based Learning (DGBL) are widely recognised as effective methods to enhance bilingual education, their combination often leads to cognitive overload and fragmented learning experiences. In Taiwan's bilingual education context, where integrating English into subject teaching is a national priority, finding effective instructional models remains a critical issue. To address this, the present study introduces the Concept Map-Facilitated Content and Language Integrated Digital Gaming (CM-CLDG) model, aiming to enhance bilingual science learning for elementary students by embedding concept mapping into a digital role-playing game. Objective: Although DGBL has demonstrated potential to increase motivation and engagement, prior studies suggest that without structured guidance, learning outcomes may vary. The CM-CLDG model was designed to scaffold knowledge construction and reduce cognitive overload by integrating concept maps directly into the gaming tasks. This study aims to evaluate the effects of the CM-CLDG approach on students' English and science learning achievements, motivation, flow experience, anxiety and behavioural patterns. Method: A quasi-experimental design was adopted with 78 sixth-grade students from an elementary school in central Taiwan. Participants were divided into the CM-CLDG group and the conventional CLIL gaming (C-CLDG) group. Pre-and posttests, questionnaires, behavioural log analyses and interviews were conducted to collect triangulated data. Learning behaviours were examined using sequential analysis via GSEQ. Results and Conclusions: The CM-CLDG group significantly outperformed the C-CLDG group in both English and science achievements. Although no significant differences were found in motivation or anxiety, the C-CLDG group experienced greater flow. Behavioural analysis revealed that the CM-CLDG group exhibited more reflective, structured and strategic learning patterns. Interview findings supported these results, highlighting better memory retention and self-directed learning in the CM-CLDG group. These findings confirm that concept maps, when embedded in digital gameplay, can enhance bilingual learning outcomes and support more effective learning behaviours in CLIL-based educational games.

segments.sourceText: Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) has gained increasing attention in recent years as an effective instructional approach for promoting bilingual competence and subject learning simultaneously (Coyle et al. 2010; Jafarigohar et al. 2025). Based on the four Cs framework (Content, Communication, Cognition and Culture), CLIL has been widely adopted in European and Asian educational systems. In Taiwan, the government has promoted the ‘Bilingual 2030’ policy to integrate English into various subject areas in elementary and secondary schools. Despite its theoretical appeal, CLIL faces persistent challenges, including excessive cognitive load for learners, insufficient scaffolding for linking language with subject content and difficulties in sustaining engagement in cognitively demanding tasks (Dalton-Puffer 2011; Wong and Tian 2025). These limitations highlight the need for supportive pedagogical tools that can more effectively structure content-language integration.

segments.sourceText: In response to these issues, digital game-based learning (DGBL) has been proposed as a promising approach to support CLIL implementation in primary education. DGBL environments, characterised by interactive tasks, immediate feedback and immersive storylines, have been found to foster motivation and engagement among young learners (Gee 2003; van Eck 2006). Studies have reported the benefits of integrating computer games into language and content instruction, showing improvements in motivation, attention and participation (Bourgonjon et al. 2010; Inal and Cagiltay 2007). However, other researchers have cautioned that without proper instructional scaffolds, game-based activities may fail to produce significant learning gains (Charsky and Mims 2008; Fisch 2005). In particular, game-based tasks often lead to fragmented knowledge construction, as learners may focus on gameplay mechanics rather than building explicit connections between language and subject content. This indicates that DGBL needs to be complemented with structured tools to guide learners' cognitive processes and strengthen content-language integration.

segments.sourceText: Moreover, the arbitrary or poorly aligned use of learning strategies within games can undermine the learning experience. For instance, Charsky and Ressler (2011) observed that students required to use external tools for knowledge construction during gameplay exhibited lower motivation. These findings underscore the importance of embedding instructional strategies into game mechanics and narratives rather than treating them as add-ons. Among various instructional strategies, concept mapping is particularly noteworthy because it provides a visual and structural means for learners to organise complex relationships between language and content. Unlike other strategies that may feel peripheral to gameplay, concept maps can serve as an integral scaffold by externalising cognitive processes and making implicit knowledge connections explicit (Novak and Cañas 2008). Therefore, selecting concept mapping as the embedded strategy aims to address the problem of fragmented learning while minimising the risk of disengagement caused by unrelated external tools.

translation.faithfulZh: 此外，在遊戲中任意或不一致地使用學習策略會破壞學習體驗。 例如，Charsky 和 Ressler (2011) 觀察到，在遊戲過程中需要使用外部工具進行知識構建的學生表現出較低的動力。 這些發現強調了將教學策略嵌入遊戲機制和敘述中的重要性，而不是將它們視為附加元件。 在各種教學策略中，概念對映特別值得注意，因為它為學習者提供了一種視覺和結構的手段，以組織語言和內容之間的複雜關係。 與其他可能在遊戲玩法中感覺到的策略不同，概念圖可以透過將認知過程外化並使隱式知識連結成為一個完整的支架（Novak 和 Cañas 2008）。 因此，選擇概念對映作為嵌入式策略旨在解決分散學習的問題，同時最大限度地減少由無關的外部工具引起的脫離風險。

segments.sourceText: However, even when concept mapping strategies are embedded within the game narrative, their impact on learners' engagement and flow may vary. Hwang et al. (2013) found that while students using a concept map-embedded educational game showed significantly better learning achievement and lower cognitive load, their overall motivation and flow experience did not significantly differ from those who played a conventional game. One possible explanation is that concept mapping, despite aiding in knowledge organisation, may interrupt the immersive flow of gameplay due to its reflective and analytical nature. This aligns with Charsky and Ressler's (2011) argument that cognitive scaffolds, if overly effortful or externally imposed, can disrupt students' autonomy and enjoyment, ultimately reducing the affective benefits of game-based learning.

In a bilingual science learning context, concept maps can serve both as content organisers and language scaffolds, supporting the dual goals of CLIL instruction. By embedding concept map construction tasks within gaming missions, learners can contextualise vocabulary, reinforce scientific concepts and articulate their understanding within the game environment.

segments.sourceText: DGBL is an educational approach that integrates game mechanics and learning objectives to engage students in meaningful learning tasks (Hwang et al. 2020; Panjaburee et al. 2025; Prensky 2007). In DGBL environments, learners interact with computer-based games where educational content is embedded within gaming scenarios, guiding learners to accomplish tasks through exploration, decision-making and problem-solving (Poompimol et al. 2024; Prensky 2007). These games are often designed to create immersive learning experiences by offering challenges that foster cognitive development and skill acquisition, with the support of instant feedback mechanisms that promote reflection and revision (Kinzie and Joseph 2008; Oblinger 2004). Learners are typically required to complete missions or solve problems that align with educational goals,

segments.sourceText: In recent years, many researchers have explored the effectiveness of DGBL in terms of enhancing different aspects of student learning, including learning achievement, motivation, flow experience, anxiety and learning behaviour. For instance, Hwang et al. (2020) conducted a meta-analysis on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education and found that DGBL had a significant positive impact on students' academic achievement. Other studies (e.g., Chen and Hwang 2020; Hwang and Zou 2020) have shown that DGBL enhances students' learning motivation through personalised or gamified designs. The use of digital games has also been associated with improved flow experience, where students become deeply engaged in tasks. Furthermore, DGBL has demonstrated potential in reducing learning anxiety, especially when incorporating adaptive feedback or agent-based systems. In terms of behaviour, recent studies have analysed learning logs and behaviour patterns to evaluate how students interact with game elements, make decisions and adjust strategies during gameplay.

(2020) 對科學、技術、工程和數學 (STEM) 教育進行了薈萃分析，發現 DGBL 對學生的學業成績有顯著的積極影響。 其他研究（例如，Chen 和 Hwang 2020；Hwang 和 Zou 2020）表明，DGBL 透過個性化或遊戲化設計增強了學生的學習動力。 數字遊戲的使用也與改善流動體驗有關，學生深入參與任務。 此外，DGBL 已經證明了在減少學習焦慮方面的潛力，尤其是在結合自適應回饋或基於代理的系統時。 在行為方面，最近的研究分析了學習日誌和行為模式，以評估學生如何與遊戲元素互動、做出決定和調整遊戲過程中的策略。

segments.sourceText: However, despite its advantages, DGBL also faces several challenges in educational practice. One concern is the alignment of game mechanics with pedagogical objectives. Without careful integration, learners may focus more on winning the game rather than on acquiring knowledge (Charsky and Ressler 2011). Moreover, game design that lacks adequate scaffolding or personalised support may result in increased cognitive load or disengagement (Ke 2008). Additionally, there are issues related to assessment, as traditional evaluation methods may not fully capture the depth of learning occurring in game-based environments (Nelson et al. 2011). As such, it is crucial to embed effective instructional strategies and assessment tools within DGBL environments to ensure that educational goals are met while maintaining the motivational appeal of games.

translation.faithfulZh: 然而，儘管 DGBL 具有優勢，但在教育實踐中也面臨著一些挑戰。 一種擔憂是遊戲機制與教學目標的對齊。 如果沒有仔細的整合，學習者可能會更專注於贏得遊戲而不是獲取知識（Charsky 和 Ressler 2011）。 此外，缺乏足夠的腳手架或個性化支援的遊戲設計可能會導致認知負荷或脫離的增加（Ke 2008）。 此外，還有與評估相關的問題，因為傳統的評估方法可能無法完全捕捉到基於遊戲環境的學習深度（Nelson et al. 2011）。 因此，在 DGBL 環境中嵌入有效的教學策略和評估工具以確保在保持遊戲的激勵吸引力的同時實現教育目標至關重要。
translation.plainZh: 儘管有其優勢，但 DGBL 面臨著將遊戲機制與教學法保持一致的挑戰，以避免將勝利置於學習的優先順序。 沒有腳手架的糟糕遊戲設計會導致認知負荷增加或脫離。 評估方法也難以在基於遊戲的環境中完全捕獲學習。

segments.sourceText: Concept maps are visual learning tools that enable learners to represent, organise and connect their understanding of knowledge domains through diagrams that illustrate the relationships among concepts (Novak and Gowin 1984; Novak et al. 1983). By organising concepts hierarchically and showing linkages between them, concept maps help learners clarify complex ideas, identify misconceptions and support meaningful learning (Chiou 2008). In instructional contexts, concept maps have been widely used as tools for knowledge construction (Hwang and Zou 2020), learning diagnosis (Chang et al. 2005) and formative assessment (Cai et al. 2025). Their application has spanned multiple disciplines, including science, language education and computer programming.

translation.faithfulZh: 概念圖是視覺化學習工具，使學習者能夠透過說明概念之間關係的圖表來表示、組織和連線他們對知識領域的理解（Novak 和 Gowin 1984；Novak et al. 1983）。 透過分層組織概念並顯示它們之間的聯絡，概念圖可以幫助學習者澄清複雜的想法，識別誤解並支援有意義的學習（Chio 2008）。 在教學環境中，概念圖已被廣泛用作知識構建（Hwang 和 Zou 2020）、學習診斷（Chang et al. 2005）和形成性評估（Cai et al. 2025）的工具。 他們的應用跨越了多個學科，包括科學、語言教育和電腦程式設計。

segments.sourceText: Recent studies have investigated the effectiveness of concept maps in terms of supporting various learning outcomes, with multiple studies showing significant benefits for learning achievement (Chang et al. 2022; Huang et al. 2022; Hwang and Zou 2020; Kienitz et al. 2025). For example, Chen and Hwang (2020) found that a concept mapping-based flipped classroom improved English learners' speaking performance. As for learning motivation, the visual and integrative nature of concept mapping has been found to enhance learners' engagement and perceived usefulness of tasks (Novak and Cañas 2008; Sun and Lee 2016). Moreover, Huang et al. (2022) indicated that students using concept mapping strategies in science inquiry displayed higher levels of motivation and participation. Regarding learning anxiety, research is relatively limited. However, Chen and Hwang (2020) reported that students in concept mapping-based environments showed reduced speaking anxiety. While fewer studies have directly linked concept maps to reductions in learning anxiety, the structure and clarity they provide may indirectly mitigate confusion-related stress. In terms of learning behaviour, studies have applied behaviour sequence analysis and learning log interpretation to understand how students engage with concept maps. Kienitz et al. (2025) and Hwang and Zou (2020) found that learners using concept maps exhibited more strategic and reflective learning behaviours. Chang et al. (2022) further summarised that concept maps help scaffold self-regulated learning behaviours across K-12 settings. It is worth noting that while concept maps have been widely used to support various learning outcomes, research directly linking concept maps to flow experience is currently limited. This represents a gap in the literature. Given that flow experience is characterised by deep engagement and immersion, future studies could explore how concept mapping strategies, especially when integrated with interactive environments like games, may facilitate flow among learners.

segments.sourceText: While prior studies have respectively examined the benefits of DGBL and concept mapping, research that integrates these two approaches remains scarce, not to mention in CLIL contexts. DGBL has been widely recognised for enhancing motivation and engagement, yet it often results in fragmented knowledge construction and insufficient scaffolding for integrating subject content during the gaming process (e.g., Zhao et al. 2025). Without explicit structural support, learners may struggle to connect in-game experiences with underlying disciplinary concepts, leading to surface-level or disjointed understanding. Concept mapping, by contrast, provides an evidence-based means of externalising cognitive processes, reducing extraneous cognitive load and strengthening coherence among concepts (Cheng et al. 2024; Chu et al. 2025). Prior research has demonstrated its effectiveness in terms of promoting meaningful learning by making relationships between ideas visible and facilitating reflection (Chang et al. 2016). Embedding concept mapping into DGBL, therefore, offers a theoretically grounded solution to address the shortcomings of game-based environments. Specifically, it can scaffold learners in constructing integrative knowledge, support bilingual content-language connections and guide them toward more reflective and strategic learning behaviours. This rationale directly underpins the design of the CM-CLDG model.

segments.sourceText: In this study, a concept map-facilitated content and language-integrated digital gaming model is proposed by embedding concept mapping strategies into gaming scenarios to facilitate students' learning performance in an integrated English and science course for EFL (English as a Foreign Language) students. The digital game, ‘SF Queen's Adventure’, was implemented using the RPG Maker platform developed by Enterbrain Incorporation. Figure 1 illustrates the structure of the concept map-embedded digital game, including a gaming module, a concept mapping module, a gaming rule database, a gaming depository database, a learning materials database and a set of predefined concept maps. Throughout gameplay, students interact with the Queen character, who provides guidance and assigns missions to collect badges within various habitat environments. Their learning portfolios, including completed and uncompleted missions, badges collected during the exploration of habitats, and responses to embedded quiz questions, are systematically recorded in the gaming depository database. Subsequently, the concept mapping module assists learners in organising and structuring the collected data according to concept map templates designed and provided by instructors, enabling them to effectively integrate knowledge and language skills within the game's narrative context.

abstract.faithfulZh: 背景技術解決問題的能力是學生在21世紀發展的一項重要技能。 許多先前的研究都集中在各種數字教育遊戲對解決問題能力的影響上。 然而，研究結果不一致，一些研究報告了基於數字遊戲的學習 (DGBL) 對解決問題的能力的積極影響，而另一些研究發現沒有顯著的改善或報告的負面影響。 目的 本研究的目的是進行三層次的薈萃分析，以研究DGBL對問題解決能力的影響。 此外，該研究旨在檢查各種調節因素，以探索主要研究中潛在不一致的來源。 方法 透過系統的文獻檢索，確定了 21 項主要研究，包括總共 60 個效應大小。 該分析涉及評估 DGBL 在提高學生解決問題能力和檢查研究之間的異質性方面的有效性。 還進行了調節分析，以探索不同因素對 DGBL 有效性的影響。 結果和結論 結果表明，DGBL 可以有效地增強學生的問題解決能力（g = 0.654），在研究中觀察到顯著的異質性（Q = 858.358，p < 0.001）。 此外，我們的研究結果表明，與專注於解決問題的技能的研究（g = 0.440）相比，關注問題解決能力感知（g = 1.498）的研究產生的效果顯著更大。 此外，與單獨使用 DGBL 相比，將相關教學策略與 DGBL (g = 1.246) 相結合的效果顯著更好 (g = 0.399)。 對調節因子的分析表明，效應量受到教學策略和問題解決結構的顯著影響。 其他檢查的調節因素對不一致的發現沒有顯示出顯著影響。

abstract.faithfulZh: 使用電腦遊戲能提高學生學習課堂材料的動力嗎？ 當前的研究考察了學生在玩商業化、現成的電腦遊戲《文明 III》的同時學習歷史概念的動機。 該研究檢查了使用概念性腳手架伴隨遊戲玩法的效果。 來自三個九年級教室的學生被分配到三組中的一組：一組使用專家生成的概念圖，一組構建了自己的概念圖，一個對照組不使用地圖。 預計使用概念圖將提高遊戲活動的教育價值，特別是學生的動機水平； 然而，相反的情況發生了。 使用概念圖的學生相對於他們定期課堂教學的基線動機表現出較低的任務動機。 相比之下，對於對照組的學生，玩遊戲的動機水平在常規課堂教學中達到或超過了他們的動力水平。 這些結果表明，使用概念性腳手架會降低學生透過遊戲學習學習課堂材料的動機，這可能是因為概念圖可以（a）將學生的注意力集中在學習概念的難度和對玩遊戲的外部獎勵上，以及（b）使遊戲的玩法不那麼自主，更少創造性，以及 不太活躍。 所有這些都可以否定提供發揮其主要潛在教學力量的主要屬性：樂趣。 （包含 4 個表和 8 個數字。）

abstract.faithfulZh: 本文關注的是決定材料難度的一些因素。 建議在考慮智力活動時，模式獲取和自動化是學習的主要機制。 簡要總結了認知負荷理論對資訊結構的影響，以透過將認知活動集中在模式獲取上來減少難度。 有人指出，認知負荷理論涉及人為的學習和解決問題的難度，因為它可以透過教學設計來操縱。 相比之下，內在認知負荷對於給定區域是恆定的，因為它是材料的基本組成部分。 內在認知負荷的特點是元素互動性。 大多數模式的元素必須同時學習，因為它們相互作用，關鍵是互動。 如果，就像在某些領域一樣，必須學習許多元素之間的相互作用，那麼內在的認知負荷就會很高。 相比之下，在不同的領域，如果元素可以連續而不是同時學習，因為它們不相互作用，內在的認知負荷將很低。 建議僅干擾學習的外來認知負荷是高元素互動性導致的高認知負荷條件下的問題。 在低元素互動性的條件下，重新設計指令以減少無關的認知負荷可能不會產生明顯的後果。 此外，元素互動性的概念不僅可以用來解釋為什麼有些材料難以學習，而且還可以用來解釋為什麼很難理解。 當必須學習具有自然高認知負荷的高元素互動性材料時，理解變得相關。

abstract.faithfulZh: 基於數字遊戲的學習是一個以學生為中心的學習環境，它影響學習成功和學習動機。 然而，設計不佳的教學遊戲會損害學習。 透過廣泛的知識構建和高參與度，協作概念對映策略有可能解決上述問題。 同時，教學的第一原則可以進一步提高協作概念對映的有效性。 因此，針對中國八年級學生在生物學課程中提出了一種利用教學方法的第一原則的基於協作知識組織者的數字遊戲。 本研究採用準實驗設計，由 92 名學生組成的三組：基於協作知識組織者的數字遊戲 (CKO-DG) 組 (n = 33)、基於知識組織者的數字遊戲 (KO-DG) 組 (n = 31)，以及 協作數字遊戲 (CDG) 組 (n = 28)。 研究結果表明，CKO-DG 的學生取得了最好的生物學成就和動機。 然而，KO-DG 學生缺乏同伴支援，導致更高的認知負荷； CDG 學生缺乏適當的策略來組織他們的知識，從而導致學習成果低。
